items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: And there was a fellow named Ainkion (phonetic), very handsome fellow. He was a Czechoslovakian. He could play a lot of saxaphone.

ctx.x: would come to work, and he would come to work, he would have about seven cousins or relatives, or something, they'd all be there and then, one night, you don't see nobody there. Then one night you would see Tango in there by himself and the French fellow who played the bass was called Vola.

Now, when we would get finished, we'd have jam sessions. And there was a fellow named Ainkion (phonetic), very handsome fellow. He was a Czechoslovakian. He could play a lot of saxaphone. He could play a lot of saxaphone and he had another boy named Alex Campbell. He could play a lot of tenor saxophone.
Ainkion, he had heard Benny Carter but he was playing his own style and then we had a fellow who had been over there a long time, a trumpet player and he used to play a lot of trumpet.
